obligations.statement: allocate runs only when power_of_two(alignment) and alignment <= alignment_limit and size <= largest_request; otherwise returns null, unchanged.
premises: the generated predicate is the clause (tools/ic_declarations.py writes both from one text)
the guard's arguments are the declared parameters (as read at each site)
obligations.method: source structure: each call of the predicate guards the declared refusal

obligations.statement: Unless power_of_two(alignment) and alignment <= alignment_limit and size <= largest_request, allocate changes nothing observable.
premises: a const local's initializer changes nothing observable (it reads)
an earlier guard's refusal path ends in a return
obligations.method: source structure: only const locals, guards and their refusals precede the guard in its function

obligations.statement: A stale identity (block address: the start of a live block) is refused: returns Release::refused, changing nothing observable.
For any number of threads, pages and blocks and any interleaving, the page protocol never reaches an integrity stop, never refuses a held block's release, and keeps its invariant.
premises: each segment between step marks atomic
obligations.method: sxv's: read the step routines from the source, cut at STX_MINMALLOCPP_STEP marks, discharge each path algebraically (counters as finite sums with three elementary laws, popcount by its algebra). The method is credited to the allocator study of 2026-11-18 (stxlib_notes, planning/stx_minmallocpp/SXV_EVALUATION.md); sxv itself stays study-only (owner, IC decision 6).

obligations.statement: A release of an address that is not the start of a live block is refused without reading or writing the address or anything near it.
take_from keeps a page's count: the lowest free bit leaves the word and live grows by one.
premises: take_from runs on a non-zero word (its caller loaded it and found it non-zero)
the step is atomic (between step marks)
obligations.method: sxv's: the sum updated at one word; pop(x & (x - 1)) = pop(x) - 1 for x != 0 (the counter and popcount algebra is the allocator study's sxv (stxlib_notes, planning/stx_minmallocpp/SXV_EVALUATION.md, 2026-11-18), re-implemented here; sxv stays study-only (owner, IC decision 6))

obligations.statement: The owner's release keeps a page's count and never takes live below zero: the block's bit joins its word and live falls by one.
premises: the block is live (its bit is clear in the word, checked by the integrity stop before the store)
a live block counts in live, so live >= 1
the step is atomic (between step marks)
obligations.method: sxv's: the sum updated at one word; pop(a | b) = pop(a) + pop(b) for disjoint a and b; pop of one bit is 1 (the counter and popcount algebra is the allocator study's sxv (stxlib_notes, planning/stx_minmallocpp/SXV_EVALUATION.md, 2026-11-18), re-implemented here; sxv stays study-only (owner, IC decision 6))

obligations.statement: Collecting the remotely released blocks of a word keeps a page's count and never takes live below zero.
premises: the integrity stops before the store end the process when the words overlap or the count exceeds live
the step is atomic (between step marks)

obligations.statement: A page made with its blocks free starts with its count: its full words and its last word's low bits are its capacity, and live is zero.
premises: the plan's words are the capacity in 64-bit words, rounded up, so every word but the last is full (remaining >= 64) and the last holds 1 to 64 blocks
a word with remaining >= 64 is u64_max, the last 2^remaining - 1 (or u64_max when remaining is 64)
obligations.method: sxv's: a finite sum split at its last term; pop of all 64 bits is 64; pop(2^r - 1) = r (the counter and popcount algebra is the allocator study's sxv (stxlib_notes, planning/stx_minmallocpp/SXV_EVALUATION.md, 2026-11-18), re-implemented here; sxv stays study-only (owner, IC decision 6))
